useCase.summary: Read and create Linear issues from an agent on behalf of a user.

verdict.headline: Linear needs your own OAuth app but has no documented review, so you can connect within an hour.
verdict.startToday: Create the Linear OAuth2 application now; it is the only step with a real dependency and takes about 10 minutes.

composio.why: Composio has a managed OAuth2 app for Linear, so you can test immediately; register your own OAuth app before production if you want your own branding on the consent screen.

requirements.item: A Linear workspace account that can create OAuth applications

steps.title: Decide scopes
steps.detail: Pick the narrowest scopes: `read` for listing, `write` for edits, `issues:create` for creating issues. Avoid `admin`.

steps.title: Check Composio managed Linear toolkit
steps.detail: Look up the `linear` toolkit in Composio; managed OAuth2 is available, so you can test without your own app.

steps.title: Create an OAuth2 application
steps.detail: Sign in to Linear as a workspace member and open **Settings > API > OAuth applications > New**. Enter name, developer name and description.

steps.title: Add the Composio redirect URL
steps.detail: Paste the Composio callback URL into the application's redirect callback URLs and save.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret into Composio (own app)
steps.detail: Create a Composio auth config for `linear` with your own client ID and client secret and the chosen scopes. Never commit the secret.

steps.title: Run the first OAuth connection
steps.detail: Initiate a connection, approve the consent screen in Linear, and confirm the connection shows ACTIVE.

steps.title: Verify a tool call
steps.detail: Execute a read-only Linear tool (e.g. list issues) with the new connection and check the response.

steps.title: Plan for token refresh
steps.detail: Access tokens last 24 hours; Composio refreshes them for managed connections, but confirm refresh works for your own app before going live.

steps.title: Optional: enable PKCE
steps.detail: If you run your own OAuth client outside Composio, use PKCE with S256.

risks.title: Access tokens expire after 24 hours
risks.symptom: 401 from the Linear API after a day
risks.fix: Ensure refresh tokens are stored and refreshed; Composio handles this when connected through it.

risks.title: Redirect URL mismatch
risks.symptom: redirect_uri mismatch error on the consent screen
risks.fix: Make the Linear redirect URL exactly equal the Composio callback URL.

claims.text: OAuth2 applications are created in Linear's API settings at linear.app/settings/api/applications/new, where redirect callback URLs are configured.
Authorization goes to https://linear.app/oauth/authorize and tokens are exchanged at https://api.linear.app/oauth/token.
Linear scopes include read (default), write, issues:create, comments:create and admin; admin should only be requested if absolutely needed.

sources.title: Linear Developers: OAuth 2.0 authentication
sources.quote: `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. `write` - Write access for the user's account. `issues:create` - Allows creating new issues and their attachments. `comments:create` - Allows creating new issue comments. `admin` - Full access to admin level endpoints. You should never ask for this permission unless it's absolutely needed

claims.text: Access tokens are valid for 24 hours and must be refreshed.

sources.title: Linear Developers: OAuth 2.0 authentication
sources.quote: The access token is valid for 24 hours and will need to be refreshed when it expires.

claims.text: The OAuth documentation describes no app review or approval step; the app can be used right after creation.
Linear supports PKCE with plain or S256 code challenge methods.
Composio has managed OAuth2 for Linear (composio_managed_auth_schemes includes OAUTH2).
The whole own-app setup takes roughly 15-30 minutes of hands-on work.
Registering the Composio callback URL as a Linear redirect URL is required for Composio to complete the OAuth exchange.

openQuestions: Are there workspace-level restrictions on who can create OAuth apps?
